candidates.title: RAW temporary cleansing changes a quality while lead remains lead despite silver-like appearance

source_basis.locus: id00103 complete lead paragraph, within owned ChapterI
source_basis.quote: And with wiping and cleansing, this uncleanness of lead may be taken away for a time, but never for always; a man may wipe off the uncleanness but alway it is lead although it seemeth silver. But strange qualities have mastery therein and beguile men, and make them err therein.

candidates.complete_focal_source:
Of lead are two manner of kinds, white and black, and the white is the
better, and was first found in the islands of the Atlantic Sea in old
time, and is now found in many places. For in France and in Portugal
is a manner of black earth found full of gravel and of small stones,
and is washed and blown, and so of that matter cometh the substance of
lead. Also in gold quarries with matter of gold are small stones
found, and are gathered with the gold, and blown by themselves, and
turn all to lead, and therefore gold is as heavy as lead. But of black
lead is double kind. For black lead cometh alone of a vein, or is
gendered of silver in medlied veins, and is blown, and in blowing
first cometh tin, and then silver, and then what leaveth is blown and
turneth into black lead. Aristotle saith that of brimstone that is
boisterous and not swiftly pured, but troublous and thick, and of
quicksilver, the substance of lead is gendered, and is gendered in
mineral places; so of uncleanness of impure brimstone lead hath a
manner of neshness, and smircheth his hand that toucheth it. And with
wiping and cleansing, this uncleanness of lead may be taken away for a
time, but never for always; a man may wipe off the uncleanness but
alway it is lead although it seemeth silver. But strange qualities
have mastery therein and beguile men, and make them err therein. Some
men take Sal Ammoniac (to cleanse it) as Aristotle saith, and
assigneth the cause of this uncleanness and saith, that in boisterous
lead is evil quicksilver heavy and fenny. Also that brimstone thereof
is evil vapour and stinking. Therefore it freezeth not well at full.
Hermes saith that lead in boiling undoeth the hardness of all sad and
hard bodies, and also of the stone adamant. Aristotle speaketh of lead
in the Meteorics and saith that lead without doubt when it is molten
is as quicksilver, but it melteth not without heat, and then all that
is molten seemeth red. Wonder it is that though lead be pale or brown,
yet by burning or by refudation of vinegar oft it gendereth seemly
colour and fair, as tewly, red, and such other; therewith women paint
themselves for to seem fair of colour.

The source attributes lead generation and impurity/softness to brimstone and quicksilver, and says touching it soils the hand.
Wiping or cleansing may remove its uncleanness for a time; the removal is not permanent.
The retained material is still lead even while it seems silver; strange qualities mislead people.
Sal ammoniac is mentioned for cleaning, followed by attributed impurity/freezing explanations.
The paragraph retains attributed softening/hardness claims, heating/melting requirements and cosmetic color uses.

IS_KIND and SEEMS_KIND share m and a kind argument while producing different commitment types. The source repeated lead expressions and cleansing/seeming/observer clauses supply actual reuse duties, not an arbitrary agent label. No EVA part is assigned BE/SEEM here.
candidates.non_tautological_consequence: TEMPORARY_REMOVAL(q,m) AND IS_KIND(m,lead) AND SEEMS_KIND(m,silver) can hold together. A rule that turns removal into silver transmutation, turns seeming into identity, or assigns nonpermanence to lead existence contradicts this source conjunction. The material cannot be replaced by the observer as the owner of silver appearance or impurity.

candidates.historical_plausibility: Owned Steele anthology preserves a selected older encyclopedic account of substances, extraction, alchemical claims and cosmetics; this is a concrete technical-description prior. The modern anthology/editorial frame is not a newly collated medieval witness or proof of target register.
source_limits: The identity/surface distinction is explicit; the particular causal path from wiping to silver appearance is context-linked, not asserted with a because clause. No microscopic explanation is supplied.
The account asserts generic possibilities and limits, not two controlled observations or a measured time until impurity returns.
Lead's other asserted effects and its comparison when molten to quicksilver remain in the full paragraph. A simile does not silently reclassify its material.

concrete_account: Some people believe donr is a stone because a stone often falls with it in severe weather.
The author calls that identity untrue, while retaining the reported co-falling ground.
If it were a stone, humans and animals killed by it would have wounds like victims of other falling stones.
The claimed observation says human victims have no wounds but are blackened at the strike.
The source attributes their death without wounds to hot vapour burning them and blood in their hearts.
